source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and I2C switches on both carrier boards
source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC run `i2cdetect -y -q 5` and forced `i2cget -f -y 5 0x73`; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic evidence/photo and unexpected-log checks; no two-board topology, switch instances, expected control byte or downstream proof.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; invents probing/soldering and discards a remote switch-state check.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/CHANGED; notices one response cannot prove both boards and flags `-f`, but still makes unsourced physical probing mandatory instead of defining per-instance functional evidence.
source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and I2C Switches on both carrier boards
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2cdetect -y -q 5 i2cget -f -y 5 0x73
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and I2C Switches on both carrier boards — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify BMC I2C-6 reaches the I2C switch on each carrier board and that each switch exposes the expected identity/control state and downstream endpoints without changing routing.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping of BMC I2C-6 to Linux bus5 and both carrier-board switch instances
Method to distinguish/select board A and board B if both use0x73
Switch part/revision, control-register semantics and expected read byte/mask for each board
PID-defined non-mutating downstream endpoint/address/reply matrix per carrier board
Kernel/daemon driver binding and whether force access is permitted
Timeout/NACK/error criteria, route-state preservation/restoration and independent BMC recovery
test_case.test_command: Map BMC I2C-6 to bus5 and identify both carrier-board switch instances, including mux/segment selection if they share0x73; capture driver ownership and routing state; read each switch control byte through the supported path; validate expected value/mask and PID-defined downstream address-specific replies per board; preserve routing and confirm sibling board/BMC health.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

Approve/replace broad scan and `-f`, define ownership, timeouts, no-route-change verification/restoration and recovery; confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.
safety_gate: Do not assume one0x73 ACK represents both boards
Do not use quick-write discovery broadly; query only approved instances/endpoints
Avoid `-f` while a switch driver/daemon owns the device unless explicitly approved
Read but do not change channel/routing control; record and verify original state
Abort on instance ambiguity, state change, NACK, timeout, stuck bus, downstream loss or BMC degradation
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-6/bus5 and board-A/board-B switch selection paths
Both carrier-board and switch part/revision identities plus owner/driver state
Original and expected switch control-byte matrix for each selected instance
Per-board downstream endpoint expected-versus-observed read matrix with timestamps/status
Evidence selection/routing did not change and sibling board remained reachable
Pre/post BMC/bus health plus engineer verdict for each board and overall
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy requires controller/bus, each target instance/address, expected replies and OOB recovery. Multi-instance aliasing must be explicitly resolved rather than inferred from one address.

source_conflict.reason: The source asks for two switches but supplies one ambiguous0x73 read and no expected value or downstream criteria. It also omits instance selection/ownership and earlier reviews invent physical probing.
